items.followUp: State the five kingdoms and give one characteristic of each.

rubric.why: Identifies key criteria used to establish the five-kingdom classification.
rubric.description: Names at least two classification criteria.
rubric.how: Award for naming at least two appropriate criteria, such as cell structure, body organization, mode of nutrition, reproduction or evolutionary relationships.

rubric.why: Cell type separates prokaryotic Monera from the eukaryotic kingdoms.
rubric.how: Award for stating that Monera is prokaryotic and the other four kingdoms are eukaryotic.

rubric.why: Level of body organization is one basis for distinguishing kingdoms.
rubric.how: Award for identifying both levels of organization.

rubric.why: Mode of nutrition distinguishes groups such as plants, animals and fungi.
rubric.description: Explains the use of mode of nutrition in classification.
rubric.how: Award for identifying autotrophic and heterotrophic nutrition or giving a correct kingdom example for each.

modelAnswer: R. H. Whittaker proposed the five-kingdom classification using cell structure, body organization, mode of nutrition, reproduction and evolutionary relationships.
Monera consists of prokaryotic organisms, while the other four kingdoms consist of eukaryotes.
Organisms may be unicellular or multicellular; their level of body organization is considered.
Mode of nutrition is also considered: plants are mainly autotrophic, while animals and fungi are heterotrophic.
